summary: The note argues that ink toner from copiers and laser printers is of very low toxicity and poses no notable hazard in an office, even when a cartridge breaks. It cites EPA testing from 1987-1988 that found low skin irritation potential, possible but non-permanent eye irritation, and respiratory exposure as the most serious hazard, with the EPA classifying toner as a nuisance dust. It also covers first aid for exposure, the environmental issue of landfill waste and recycling options, and where to find the Material Safety Data Sheet.
one_line: Explains that broken ink toner cartridges pose very low toxicity in offices, citing EPA tests, first aid steps, and recycling options.
key_facts: Ink toners used in copiers and laser printers have a very low toxicity and should not cause alarm in the office environment, even in the case of a broken toner cartridge.
The EPA conducted extensive tests on toner cartridges from January 1987 through December 1988.
The EPA tests demonstrated that the potential for skin irritation was very low.
No cases of permanent eye damage were found in the EPA tests, although eye irritation was possible.
The most serious hazard noted in the EPA tests was with respiratory exposure.
Laboratory rats exposed to 50 times the factory exposure experienced some increase in lung density.
The EPA classified ink toner as a "nuisance dust," even in the manufacturing environment.
The EPA does not classify ink toner as a carcinogen or a mutagen.
Eyes should be flushed with clean water if ink toner directly contacts the eyes.
If ink toner becomes aerosolized, the room should be cleared until the dust settles, then vacuumed with a HEPA-filtered vacuum.
The principal environmental hazard of ink toner cartridges is landfill consumption.
A discarded ink toner cartridge is not biodegradable and takes up landfill space virtually forever.
A recycled ink toner cartridge can be reused up to ten times without product degradation.
Many ink toner dealers pay several dollars each for used ink toner cartridges.
Manufacturers of ink toner cartridges are required to make the MSDS available to consumers.
